recipe_inventory.label: Choi et al. (2006): Aqueous TBA-capped PbS preparation in 1× TAE

source_locators.locator: Main PDF p. 1, aqueous synthesis and Scheme 1
SI PDF p. 1, Synthesis of PbS Quantum Dots Using Thrombin-Binding Aptamer

recipe_inventory.scope: One quantitatively charged TAE synthesis with common-family TEM range; analytical branches do not create separate syntheses.
gaps: Complete two-page main and identity-matched four-page SI, including Scheme 1, Figures 1–2 and S1–S6, 28 main and 12 SI reference entries. Cited full sources unreviewed.

Synthesis is at room temperature in open air, but numerical temperature, reaction hold time, vessel geometry, addition rate, stirring speed, precursor stock concentrations, isolation/storage protocol and yield are not reported.

The 280 µL final volume is explicitly TAE. Water pH 6.8–7.0 is a reported alternative with no significant difference, but its exact final volume and separately identified TEM specimen are not supplied.
TAE is specified as 1× without EDTA at pH 8.0; component concentrations and preparation are not given. Lead-acetate and Na2S hydration are unreported.

The estimated 430/860 nM particle concentrations assume uniform 5 nm particles. This assumed diameter is not an extra measured particle size. The 3–6 nm TEM range has no formal statistical analysis; exact buffer-versus-water image batch is unresolved.
Analytical ultracentrifugation, TEM drying, CD dilution and protein assays are separate characterization branches, not QD synthesis/purification instructions.
No measured atomic coordinates, refined crystal phase/cell or protein/aptamer conformation coordinates are supplied. Mechanistic charge transfer and chair-like quadruplex are author interpretations.
Independent source comparison passed; molecular/particle/reference-cell presentation remains pending.

source_notes.label: One aqueous route and separate analytical branches
source_notes.summary: The quantified TAE method mixes 32 nmol TBA and 125 nmol lead acetate then injects 65 nmol sulfur feed in room-temperature open air. Water is a reported alternative with unresolved final volume. TEM drying, CD dilution and ultracentrifugation belong to characterization.

SI PDF p. 1, Synthesis of PbS Quantum Dots Using Thrombin-Binding Aptamer

source_notes.label: Sulfur-reagent source conflict
source_notes.summary: Main p.1 explicitly names sodium sulfide; SI p.S1 prints sodium sulfate (Na2S), while SI p.S3 specifies S2−. The SI name/formula conflict is preserved, not silently corrected. Na2S indexes the printed formula and main identity, without resolving the inconsistent SI name or hydration.

source_notes.label: Measured and assumed dimensions
source_notes.summary: TEM typical/majority 3–6 nm has no formal statistical analysis. The uniform 5 nm diameter is assumed only to estimate 430/860 nM particle concentrations. No lattice refinement or measured coordinates are supplied.

SI PDF p. 1, Synthesis of PbS Quantum Dots Using Thrombin-Binding Aptamer

source_notes.label: Optical sensing interpretation
source_notes.summary: The authors attribute selective photobleaching to charge transfer in an aptamer/protein complex; protein absorption does not overlap QD near-infrared emission. Quadruplex and binding cartoons are interpreted conformations, not measured atomic models.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1–2, Scheme 1, Figures 1–2 and mechanistic discussion

evidence_conflicts.summary: Main p.1 explicitly names sodium sulfide; SI p.S1 prints sodium sulfate (Na2S), while SI p.S3 specifies S2−. The SI name/formula conflict is preserved, not silently corrected. Na2S indexes the printed formula and main identity, without resolving the inconsistent SI name or hydration.
